pins.title: Non-Wearable Sleep Tracker: Sleep Data Without a Ring or Watch
pins.subtitle: Under the mattress or on the nightstand
pins.description: Pull your ring off at 3 a.m., or forget to charge your watch? A non-wearable sleep tracker gives a rough picture of your sleep with nothing on your body. One kind sits under the mattress; the other uses low-power radar from the nightstand. We explain what each can and can't tell you, plus our main picks. Watch the trend over weeks, not one night. Not medical advice. Read the full guide. #sleeptracker #sleeptracking #nonwearable #bettersleep #wellnesstech

pins.title: Under Mattress Sleep Tracker vs Bedside Sensor: Which Fits Your Bed?
pins.subtitle: Your bed matters more than the spec sheet
pins.description: Under-mattress sleep tracker or bedside sensor? It depends on your bed. Withings doesn't recommend its pad for airbeds or waterbeds; a bedside sensor doesn't depend on the mattress. A pad stays out of sight, a bedside sensor sits by your pillow. Both track one sleeper, so partners or pets can affect readings, and both need an outlet nearby. Not medical advice. Compare the options. #sleeptracker #undermattress #sleeptracking #bettersleep #wellnesstech

pins.title: Non-Wearable Sleep Tracker Checklist: 6 Things to Check Before You Buy
pins.subtitle: Bed, partner, outlet, phone, Wi-Fi, subscription
pins.description: Save this before you buy a non-wearable sleep tracker. 1) What bed do you have, and how thick is the mattress? 2) Who else sleeps in the bed? 3) Is there an outlet nearby? 4) What OS version is your phone on? 5) Does your Wi-Fi reach the bedroom? 6) What can you see without a subscription? Terms may change. These are wellness trackers, not diagnostic tools. Not medical advice. Full checklist in the guide. #sleeptracker #undermattress #checklist #bettersleep
